source.title: Enabling Preference-driven Unlearning in Few-step Distilled Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
source.authors: Gaurav Patel; Jun Fang; G. V. Steeg; Qiang Qiu; Sravan Sripada

record.tranche_reason: Tests targeted concept unlearning and retention in few-step distilled text-to-image diffusion models, a different modality and setting from the LLM unlearning attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates concept suppression and non-target utility after unlearning, but does not test recovery by relearning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting. References to prompt attacks and the possibility of adversarial or paraphrased prompts are not tested results. Rows below focus on the paper’s CePU unlearning results; cited findings from other work and comparisons between other methods are not included.
record.test_reason: The study proposes and evaluates CePU, a concept-unlearning method for few-step distilled text-to-image diffusion models. Every version of the claim concerns knowledge unlearning in LLMs, such as WMDP hazardous knowledge or Harry Potter facts, and whether relearning, internal edits, quantization or prompting recovers it. Diffusion image generators are a different kind of system, and the measures are generated-image classifiers (celebrity detector, NudeNet, class accuracy), not LLM knowledge accuracy. The LLM unlearning literature, including WMDP, is only cited in related work. There are no relearning, activation-ablation or quantization attacks. The red-teaming prompt sets (P4D, MMA-A, Ring-a-Bell, SneakyPrompt) are a prompt-attack analogue, but in a different modality, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that CePU, a consistency-error reward in place of noise-prediction reward, gives effective targeted forgetting in few-step distilled T2I models. They claim strong utility retention and Pareto-favourable trade-offs across identity and nudity tasks, including red-teaming prompts, with an extension to objects. They also concede, in Broader Impacts, that unlearning does not guarantee complete removal under adversarial or paraphrased prompting. They make no claims about LLM unlearning or recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: Proposes consistency-enforced preference optimization (CePU) for few-step text-to-image diffusion models, using consistency-error rewards and a retention regularizer. It does not implement or test the specified LLM unlearning attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with model, target, prompt benchmark, β and λ; the paper reports trade-offs as β or λ changes and evaluates different numbers of sampling steps. It states that increasing λ improves utility but weakens unlearning, and that larger β weakens updates while improving utility retention.

fits_no_version.finding: In few-step diffusion models, CePU-unlearned models still yield a few NudeNet detections under red-teaming and adversarial prompt sets unseen in training (P4D, MMA-A, Ring-a-Bell, SneakyPrompt). Examples: 6 of 876 on SD-Turbo at β=500, 130 of 3120 on DS-V8 at β=500, 68 of 2554 on DS-V7 at β=100. Suppression weakens as β rises, e.g. 659 detections on DS-V7 at β=1000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models resists adversarial red-teaming prompts, with residual leakage that depends on unlearning strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Identity removal on DS-V7-LCM is incomplete at the reported setting (18.75 and 7.81 target accuracy at β=1000). It is near-complete at lower β but with lower non-target retention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept suppression in few-step diffusion models trades off against retention via the β and λ hyperparameters.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 (40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)
record.problems: The evidence is for text-to-image diffusion models, not LLMs, and does not test recovery attacks. Evaluation relies on automatic NudeNet and celebrity classifiers and perceptual metrics; the authors note these proxies are imperfect and do not report human evaluation. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Not every per-class Imagenette result or every β-sweep value is transcribed; aggregate results and selected explicit sweep outcomes are retained. Tables 1–3 and Tables E–L contain extensive per-method and per-condition comparisons. Results for competing unlearning methods are not catalogued here.

untested.parts: No LLM knowledge unlearning, no near-chance knowledge accuracy, no attack-based recovery test on LLMs.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack after unlearning.
No activation ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deletion.
No LLM prompting recovery. The diffusion red-teaming prompts are an analogue in another modality only.
CePU is not tested against relearning, ablation, quantization or LLM jailbreak recovery.

record.verdict_notes: Different modality: diffusion image generators, not LLMs. The study is better treated as cites_only/T6 for this LLM-focused phenomenon. The reader's β conditions for r7–r10 are wrong: the Table 2 CePU entries correspond to β=500 per Tables J and K. The Table 1 CePU identity entries correspond to β=1000 per Tables H and I. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether attacks recover forgotten concepts; tests suppression and utility only in text-to-image diffusion models, not LLM knowledge accuracy.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing access-blocking rather than deletion.
No post-unlearning rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context recovery test.
CePU is proposed and evaluated for unlearning effectiveness, but its resistance to the specified recovery attacks is not tested.

reader_labels.reason: Reported target identity accuracy is 0 for both targets; nudity DSR is 95.83% on DreamShaper-V8-LCM and 99.32% on SD-Turbo, and Imagenette average target accuracy is 0 (r1, r3, r7, r9, r11). The study also reports non-target accuracy and perceptual utility measures, though these are not unchanged.

reader_labels.condition: DreamShaper-V7-LCM identity targets and utility-retention measures
reader_labels.reason: Identity target accuracy remains 18.75 and 7.81 for the two targets, while non-target accuracy is below baseline in reported settings; these diffusion results do not establish resistance to recovery attacks (r2, r4, r5, r6, r8, r10, r12, r13, r15).
